edges.description: Holding the erythroid progenitor compartment out of cycle halts red-cell production, which is clinically silent where red-cell lifespan is normal and precipitates an acute aplastic crisis where it is short.
Bright red facial erythema confined to the cheeks, giving the appearance of having been slapped.

nodes.description: Viral NS1 protein and replication intermediates activate the DNA damage response (DDR) pathway, particularly ATR and DNA-PKcs, leading to late S/G2 phase arrest and apoptotic death of infected erythroid progenitor cells.

biological_processes: NS1-driven G2 checkpoint arrest of the infected progenitor

evidence.reference_title: Parvovirus B19 NS1 protein induces cell cycle arrest at G2-phase by activating the ATR-CDC25C-CDK1 pathway.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, we found that the ATR-CHK1-CDC25C-CDK1 pathway was activated during B19V infection of EPCs, and that ATR activation played an important role in B19V infection-induced G2-phase arrest.

evidence.reference_title: Parvovirus B19 NS1 protein induces cell cycle arrest at G2-phase by activating the ATR-CDC25C-CDK1 pathway.
evidence.snippet: Activated ATR phosphorylated CDC25C at serine 216, which in turn inactivated the cyclin B/CDK1 complex without affecting nuclear import of the complex.

evidence.reference_title: Parvovirus B19 and the pathogenesis of anaemia.
evidence.snippet: In addition, B19 infection induces cell cycle arrests at the G(1) and G(2) phases.

evidence.reference_title: Parvovirus B19 infection of human primary erythroid progenitor cells triggers ATR-Chk1 signaling, which promotes B19 virus replication.
evidence.snippet: B19V infection induces a broad range of DNA damage responses by triggering phosphorylation of all the upstream kinases of each of three repair pathways: ATM (ataxia-telangiectasi mutated), ATR (ATM and Rad3 related), and DNA-PKcs (DNA-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit).

nodes.description: Classic childhood exanthem characterized by facial erythema (slapped cheek) followed by lacy reticular rash on trunk and extremities.

evidence.snippet: Erythema infectiosum, the most common clinical manifestation of parvovirus B19 infection, is characterized by a 'slapped cheek' appearance on the face and lacy exanthem on the trunk and extremities.

evidence.reference_title: The cutaneous manifestations of human parvovirus B19 infection.
evidence.snippet: The prototypical cutaneous manifestations of human parvovirus B19 (B19) infection include a petechial eruption in a glove and stocking distribution, reticular truncal erythema, and the 'slapped cheek' sign.

evidence.reference_title: Erythema infectiosum and other parvovirus B19 infections.
evidence.snippet: The human parvovirus B19 has been identified as the causative agent in several diseases, including the benign childhood condition erythema infectiosum (fifth disease)...

evidence.reference_title: Pediatric parvovirus B19: spectrum of clinical manifestations.
evidence.snippet: The most common manifestation of PVB19 infection in children is erythema infectiosum (EI). Also known as fifth disease or slapped cheek syndrome, EI presents as an erythematous exanthem limited to the malar eminences that follows a mild prodromal illness.

nodes.description: Bright red malar erythema giving the face a slapped appearance, pathognomonic for erythema infectiosum.

evidence.reference_title: Parvovirus B19 infection. Associated diseases, common and uncommon.
evidence.snippet: the virus has been implicated in numerous disorders, including aplastic crisis in patients with chronic hemolytic anemia, erythema infectiosum, arthropathy, arthritis, and fetal infections.

nodes.description: Acute cessation of red blood cell production causing severe anemia in patients with underlying hemolytic disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Diverse hematologic effects of parvovirus B19 infection.
evidence.snippet: Human parvovirus B19 is linked with a broadening spectrum of hematologic disorders, including aplastic crises in the context of hemolytic anemias.

evidence.reference_title: Quantitation of human parvovirus B19 DNA in erythema infectiosum and aplastic crisis.
evidence.snippet: The serum B19V DNA load during the acute phase of aplastic crisis complicating chronic hemolytic anemia was extremely high.

evidence.reference_title: Original Research: Parvovirus B19 infection in children with sickle cell disease in the hydroxyurea era.
evidence.snippet: Parvovirus B19 infection causes transient aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease (SCD) due to a temporary interruption in the red blood cell production

evidence.reference_title: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis associated with parvovirus B19-induced aplastic crisis in a hereditary spherocytosis patient: A case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Parvovirus B19 had caused aplastic crisis and HLH.
